codeReview.summary: FTS tie ordering is fixed, but the vector retriever still lacks a deterministic secondary key before its inner LIMIT, so the original tie-stability blocker is not fully closed.

issues.description: `searchVector()` still orders the vec0 subquery by `distance` only before `LIMIT`, then applies `chunkId` ordering afterward. If more equal-distance rows exist than the fetch limit, SQLite can choose a different top-N subset across runs, so RRF rank can still drift under tie-heavy queries.

The new regression covers only two tied rows with a generous `limit` and calls `searchVector()` / `searchFts()` directly, so it does not exercise the boundary case where tied candidates exceed the fetch limit or the full hybrid `searchIndex()` path that originally surfaced the issue.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The shared search notes document the vector/FTS suffix-filter asymmetry, but they do not record the retriever top-N tie boundary nuance: vector ordering must be stabilized before the inner `LIMIT`, otherwise equal-distance rows can still be selected nondeterministically.
